routines.what: Writes a 132-byte record: byte at +0, bounded 64-byte copy at +0x42, another at +0x1, byte at +0x83, returns the base pointer. Byte-identical with no flags. The lever is term order in the index expression: row*132+i+0x42 matches, row*132+0x42+i does not. Putting the constant last lets the compiler fold 0x42 into a lea displacement and shorten the store, which changes 7 bytes.

routines.what: Returns 1 if a byte table lookup at 0xbd578+ is in [0x12,0x21) or equals 0x0a, else 0. Ten source shapes tried, all within one byte of the target.
routines.evidence: Target tail is 83 f9 0a 75 05 b9 01 00 00 00 8b c1 c3, which needs ecx to be the result register throughout. Shapes that produce movzx ecx get the branch structure wrong (7c 09 vs 7c 05); shapes that get the branches right (both 7c 05) use edx for movzx and emit an extra 2b c9. The two halves are reachable separately and not together, the same pattern result 10 in docs/decompilation-experiment.md records for the frame.

routines.evidence: Target uses c6 05 <disp> imm (mov byte [disp],imm) for all three stores. routines.what: Table lookup: returns the byte at 0xdeec5[dl].
routines.evidence: Target is movzx ebx, dl then mov bl,[ebx+0xdeec5]. The argument arrives in dl. Measured with tools/decode.js: four of the five call sites (0xfee68, 0xfeeb7, 0xfeedb, 0xff07c) write dl in the 24 bytes before the call, and the fifth (0xfef2d) reaches it from a path that set dl earlier. High C passes arguments on the stack: docs/highc-codegen.md measures that neither the framed nor the unframed convention uses registers, so no C source produces an entry that reads dl for an argument it never set.
